Calling zuutf from C

Source: vignettes/linking.Rmd
linking.Rmd

zuutf publishes its validation, transcoding and Base64 to other packages as a registered table of C functions, zuutf_api_v1. A package that uses it gets the SIMD kernels of simdutf in its own C code without vendoring simdutf, and without linking anything: the functions live in the shared object of zuutf and are found at run time.

DESCRIPTION

The consumer needs the header of zuutf to compile, and the namespace of zuutf loaded to run, so it declares both:

Imports: zuutf
LinkingTo: zuutf

NAMESPACE

Imports: alone does not load a namespace. Until that of zuutf is loaded, R_GetCCallable() finds nothing, so the consumer imports something real:

importFrom(zuutf, zuutf_info)

With roxygen, that is #' @importFrom zuutf zuutf_info anywhere in the package.

C

In exactly one C file, after the R headers, define ZUUTF_DEFINE_API_GET before including <zuutf.h>. That emits a static zuutf_api_get(), which resolves the table once and caches it:

#include <R.h>
#include <Rinternals.h>
#include <R_ext/Rdynload.h>

#define ZUUTF_DEFINE_API_GET
#include <zuutf.h>

SEXP mypkg_valid_utf8(SEXP x) {
  const zuutf_api *api = zuutf_api_get();
  zuutf_result r = api->validate_utf8((const char *) RAW(x), (size_t) XLENGTH(x));
  return Rf_ScalarLogical(r.error == ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS);
}

Other C files include <zuutf.h> alone for the types. The header includes <stddef.h> and <stdint.h> and nothing else: no simdutf header and no R header, so it compiles as C99 or C++17 anywhere.

Results, capacities and errors

Validation and conversion members return a zuutf_result. error is ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS (0) or one of the ZUUTF_ERR_* codes; count is the number of units read or written on success, the 0-based offset of the first error in input units on an input error, and the capacity that would have been enough on ZUUTF_ERR_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL.

Members that write take the capacity of the output and never write past it. The length members say how much to allocate:

size_t need = api->utf8_length_from_utf16le(src, n);   /* bytes */
char *out = (char *) R_alloc(need ? need : 1, 1);
zuutf_result r = api->utf16le_to_utf8(src, n, out, need);
if (r.error != ZUUTF_ERR_SUCCESS) {
  Rf_error("invalid UTF-16 at unit %zu", r.count + 1);
}

Conversion members expect valid input and report the first error; they replace nothing. For replacement with U+FFFD, call utf_convert() from R.

Base64 members take ZUUTF_BASE64_* flags: ZUUTF_BASE64_URL for the -_ alphabet, ZUUTF_BASE64_NO_PAD to encode without =, ZUUTF_BASE64_STRICT for RFC 4648 decoding instead of forgiving, and ZUUTF_BASE64_EITHER to decode either alphabet.

Versions

The table only grows. Members are appended, never reordered or removed, so a consumer built against an older header keeps working with a newer zuutf. A consumer that uses a member added after 0.1.0 checks for it first:

if (ZUUTF_API_HAS(api, some_later_member)) {
  /* ... */
}

If another public type ever changes shape, the registered name changes to zuutf_api_v2, and a stale consumer fails loudly in R_GetCCallable() instead of misreading results.

Threads

Every member is a pure function of its arguments and none calls into R, so a consumer may call them from its own threads. The first call in a process detects the CPU, which simdutf makes thread-safe. The kernel in use is the one zuutf_info() reports:

zuutf::zuutf_info()$kernel
#> [1] "icelake"
